title: How to Make a Fresh Herb Chimichurri in Under 3 Minutes
meta_description: Stop spending 20 minutes chopping herbs. Learn how to make fresh herb chimichurri fast using the right tools for a zesty, 3-minute sauce.
html:
There is nothing quite like a bright, zesty chimichurri to wake up a piece of grilled steak, roasted cauliflower, or a simple piece of toasted sourdough. But for many of us, the barrier to making it from scratch is the prep work. Standing over a cutting board for fifteen minutes, meticulously mincing handfuls of parsley and oregano, can make a quick weeknight dinner feel like a chore.

The secret to a great sauce isn't just the ingredients; it's the efficiency of your tools. If you want to make fresh herb chimichurri fast, you have to stop thinking about the traditional chef's knife approach for the greenery. By switching your method, you can go from a bunch of whole herbs to a finished sauce in under three minutes.

The Essential Ingredients for Quick Chimichurri

To keep this process fast, stick to the classics. You don't need fancy additions—the magic is in the balance of acid, oil, and fresh herbs. Gather these items before you start:

  • Fresh Parsley: The backbone of the sauce. Use flat-leaf for better flavor.
  • Fresh Oregano or Cilantro: Depending on your preference, these add the necessary earthy depth.
  • Garlic: Two cloves, smashed and finely minced.
  • Red Wine Vinegar: This provides the sharp punch that cuts through rich meats.
  • Extra Virgin Olive Oil: Use a high-quality oil for a smoother finish.
  • Red Pepper Flakes, Salt, and Pepper: For a hint of heat and seasoning.

How to Make Fresh Herb Chimichurri Fast With the Right Tools

The most time-consuming part of this recipe is the chopping. Many people reach for a food processor, but that often results in a muddy paste rather than a textured, vibrant sauce. To get that authentic, hand-chopped look without the arm workout, I use Herb Scissors.

These five-blade herb shears allow you to mince cilantro, chives, and basil in one snip. Instead of rocking a knife back and forth for ten minutes, you simply grab a handful of your parsley and oregano and snip them directly into your mixing bowl. Because there are five blades working simultaneously, you reduce your chopping time by about 80%.

Once your herbs are snipped, stir in your garlic, vinegar, oil, and spices. The result is a chunky, rustic consistency that holds onto the meat much better than a blended puree.

Step-by-Step 3-Minute Method

Follow these steps to get your sauce on the table before your steak even finishes resting:

  1. Prep the Base: In a small bowl, combine your minced garlic, red wine vinegar, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes. Stir them together to create a flavor base.
  2. The Quick Snip: Gather your washed and dried parsley and oregano. Use your Herb Scissors to snip the herbs directly into the bowl. Keep snipping until you have about a cup of minced greenery.
  3. Emulsify: Slowly pour in the olive oil while stirring with a fork or spoon. This ensures the oil doesn't just pool at the bottom but coats every bit of the herbs.
  4. Taste and Adjust: Give it a quick taste. If it's too acidic, add a splash more oil; if it's too bland, add a pinch more salt.

Cleaning Up Without the Hassle

One of the biggest deterrents to making fresh sauces is the cleanup. Traditional knives require a cutting board that needs scrubbing, and food processors have multiple parts that must go in the dishwasher. When you use Herb Scissors, you eliminate the cutting board entirely.

The best part about these shears is the included cleaning comb. Herbs—especially sticky ones like cilantro or parsley—tend to get wedged between the blades. A quick run-through with the comb clears out the debris in seconds, making the tool ready for your next meal without a deep scrub.

Best Ways to Serve Your Fast Chimichurri

While we usually associate this sauce with Argentinian steak, its versatility is its greatest strength. Because you can now make fresh herb chimichurri fast, you can use it as a daily condiment rather than a special-occasion sauce.

Try it as a marinade for grilled shrimp, a topping for baked salmon, or even stirred into a bowl of quinoa for a fresh lunch. If you have leftovers, store them in a glass jar in the fridge for up to a week. The flavors actually deepen after a day or two, making it an even better dip for crusty bread.

FAQ

Can I use dried herbs instead of fresh?

For a true chimichurri, fresh herbs are non-negotiable. Dried herbs lack the brightness and water content needed to balance the vinegar and oil. If you don't have fresh herbs, it's better to make a different vinaigrette than to use dried parsley.

Why do my herbs turn brown in the sauce?

Oxidation happens when herbs are bruised or exposed to air for too long. Using Herb Scissors helps prevent this because the clean, sharp cuts minimize bruising compared to a dull knife or the high-speed blades of a blender.

How do I keep the oil and vinegar from separating?

Chimichurri is a rustic sauce, so some separation is natural. However, stirring it vigorously right before serving or giving it a quick shake in a mason jar will re-emulsify the mixture for a consistent texture.
